title: transient-thread-architect-cribsheet
content:
Brain dump: Transient Thread Architect (working name) — minimal PRD cribsheet and runbook ideas.

Goal (one-liner): Give product teams a lightweight infrastructure for ephemeral conversation threads that can be checkpointed, stitched across devices, and cheaply rehydrated with graceful degradation when KV/cache warmup or capacity constraints occur.

Problem statement / why now:
- Users frequently create lots of short-lived threads (support chit-chat, ephemeral docs, search assistants). Keeping full token history per thread is expensive.
- Current session models: either full session kept (costly) or small context + poor rehydration (loses continuity).
- Need to balance unit cost, latency on resume, and perceived continuity.

Key hypotheses:
- A small checkpoint (summary + selective anchors) + lightweight KV for immediate local rehydration will recover ~80% of UX quality at <30% of token cost.
- Prioritizing recent turns and semantic anchors reduces rehydration latency by 40% vs full-prefix fetch.
- Automatic TTL-based eviction with user-visible affordance prevents runaway budgets.

User personas / stories:
- Power user (PM writing specs): "I switch machines or open a new window and expect the assistant to remember the last 5 turns and the list of pinned bullets." -> acceptance: within 500ms show a concise recap, follow-up prompts should reference pinned bullets.
- Customer support agent: "I want to rehydrate tickets quickly while keeping costs low for infrequent revisit." -> acceptance: average rehydration latency < 300 ms at p50 for cached threads.
- Casual user: "If a thread is old, I don't mind a short summary rather than full history." -> acceptance: decayed threads present a TL;DR and option to load full context.

Feature components (sketch):
1) Thread Checkpoint (micro-checkpoint): JSON blob stored in Redis/KV with fields: thread_id, last_n_summary, anchor_vectors, metadata (TTL, pinned_keys, token_count_est).-- implementation note: keep small, compress text.
2) Heuristic Anchors: choose 2–4 anchor turns: named entities, bullet lists, system instructions, pinned user bullets. Store short-span embeddings for quick similarity match.
3) Rehydration flow:
   - Fast path: client passes thread_id; routing returns cached checkpoint -> local reconstruction -> warm start with summary + anchors -> streaming continuation.
   - Slow path: checkpoint miss -> request full prefix fallback (or model-compact summary generation) -> user sees "loading longer context" affordance.
4) Affordances + UX:
   - Thread preview card with TTL + size estimate and quick "pin" to keep alive.
   - User setting: Keep threads for X days or cost-budget per-user.
5) Routing & QoS:
   - Tag requests by rehydration-mode: fast/slow. Fast mode can route to lower-cost model variants with stronger system prompt for continuity.

Telemetry / success metrics:
- Rehydration latency p50/p95, by fast/slow path.
- % of requests served by checkpoint fast path.
- Cost per resumed thread (tokens consumed vs baseline).
- User retention proxy: percent of resumed threads that produce >2 follow-ups.
- Quality proxy: % of resumed threads where assistant references pinned anchors as judged by micro-eval corpus.

Prototype experiments (MVP):
- Experiment A: Summary-first checkpoint. Save 200–300 token abstractive summary + top-3 anchor turns. Deploy to 10% traffic for web client only. Measure quality delta vs full-context for a set of prompt templates.
- Experiment B: Anchor-only cheap restore. No summary, only 3 anchors + metadata. Test in low-traffic mobile environment.
- Experiment C: TTL + user-pin UI. Soft launch to power-user cohort.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Fast-path serves >=60% of resumes in cohort.
- Median rehydration latency < 400ms (fast path).
- End-to-end cost on resumed sessions reduced by >=25% vs baseline where full prefix loaded.
- No measurable drop (>3%) in micro-eval quality for targeted prompt set.

API sketch (informal):
- POST /threads.create-checkpoint { thread_id, last_turns[], pinned:[...], user_signals:{explicit_pins:true}} -> {checkpoint_id, size_bytes, ttl}
- POST /threads.resume {checkpoint_id, resume_mode:fast|full, client_hint:device, desired_window:50} -> streaming tokens + status
- GET /threads/meta?thread_id=... -> {last_activity, ttl, estimate_cost}

Operational concerns / constraints:
- Storage: many small checkpoints -> choose LRU + TTL compaction. Budget: plan for N checkpoints per user (default 10).
- Privacy: checkpoints may contain PII; ensure KMS encryption at rest and optional customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
- Consistency: race conditions when two clients checkpoint concurrently. Solution: write-with-compare-and-swap tokens or epoching.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is canonical checkpoint schema? (compact vs rich) -> prototype both.
- Cost model: how do we bill resumed tokens vs background checkpoints? Should fine-grained credits apply? (billing owns to product ops)
- How long should default TTL be? 7d vs 30d vs user-configurable?
- Should we expose checkpoints in Console for enterprise customers (audit, export)?
- Fallback policy: when fast-path fails, automatically attempt on-device short-summary generation to reduce model hits?

Risks / failure modes:
- Checkpoint drift: summaries can become stale and cause hallucinations if model overweights them. Mitigation: label summaries as "summary" in system prompt and penalize as lower-confidence context.
- Exploding storage under heavy multi-session users. Mitigation: hard cap per-user and eviction policy.
- UX confusion if assistant claims to "remember" but omitted important turn. Provide transparent UI noting summarization/decay.

Rollout plan (quarterly-ish):
- Q1: Prototype A/B internal only (web, 10% traffic). Build primitive API and local client SDK.
- Q2: Expand to mobile desktop clients + telemetry; iterate checkpoint schema.
- Q3: Console controls for TTL and enterprise export; begin Dedicated + Private deployment validation (KMS).

Notes to self / low-priority ideas:
- Explore delta-checkpoints: store diffs instead of full small summaries to reduce size.
- Use cheap hashing of anchors + client-side verification to allow client to send only fingerprints.
- Could integrate with prefetched prompt tokens / warm endpoints for edge devices.

Quick open tasks (owner assigned in next sync):
- [ ] Write micro-eval prompt set (Rowan)
- [ ] Build Redis checkpoint prototype (Mika)
- [ ] Billing proposal sketch (Finance/Devon)
- [ ] Privacy review note (Security)

Scratch, brainstorming fragments:
- name ideas: "Threadlet", "MomentCache", "Transient Architect", "Recalllets" -> prefer something neutral.
- UX copy: "This thread is a short snapshot — expand to load full history".
- Shortcut: long-press thread -> pin -> extends TTL to 30d.

References / inspiration:
- small-checkpoint ideas from "prefetch-priming-profiles" doc (internal notes).
- related Jira: TT-1234, TT-1288 (consistency), BIL-212 (billing).

Questions for next sync with infra:
- Redis vs RocksDB vs S3+index tradeoffs. How much op QPS can we support for p10K users?
- Cost to store average 1KB checkpoint * 1M active users = ~1GB (~cheap) but retrieval QPS matters.

End — this is messy, intentionally. Will refine into a short PRD once prototype data exists.

-- anya
